Banned-user requirement Query explicitly applies WHERE banned = false before scanning results. Implemented; live privileged banned-user fixture was not altered or created.
Deactivated/blocked exclusion Redis-supplied deactivated and blocked encrypt IDs are excluded when present. Implemented
Input guard Literal quote and backslash parameters return a controlled 400 response. Correct

Method Coverage Result
Black box Public contract: success, empty result, invalid input, missing authorization, and pagination default. 5/5 expected outcomes matched

QA Testing Summary — 2026-07-29

Verdict: PASSED — authenticated, read-only dev checks returned the tester-owned bookmark folder and its saved posts correctly. The issue comment clarifies that a bookmark is deleted upstream when the post owner changes visibility to private or unlisted; therefore, list-time visibility filtering is not an active acceptance requirement. No coding bug was confirmed and no HTTP 500 occurred.

Environment Dev

Area Evidence Assessment
Route GET /bookmark/list/:sid is mapped to the bookmark-list handler. Correct
Ownership Folder lookup requires both the authenticated user_id and requested slug/ID; another user's folder does not resolve through this path. Correct
Listing Query scopes results to the resolved folder_id and authenticated user_id, sorts newest first, and applies pagination. Correct
Deleted/deactivated/blocked content Cached deactivated users, blocked users, and blocked posts are excluded when available. Implemented
Unsupported content video360 posts are excluded from the returned list and the total is adjusted accordingly. Implemented
Visibility clarification No list-time visibility predicate exists in this handler. The developer's issue comment states private/unlisted transitions delete the bookmark upstream, so no additional list-time filter is required by the current contract. Not a defect in this issue scope

Code review

Location Observation Impact Result
src/Action/V1/Likes/ListLikeComment.go The aggregate query for views_total_likes_per_comment runs when the current page has liker rows. The populated-page response returns the full aggregate, including the final partial page. PASS
Same handler The comment lookup joins the post and rejects visibility == "private" with 403. Prevents disclosure of private-post liker data, including for owner access. PASS
Same handler Likes query is ordered by lc.updated_at DESC, with Limit and Offset. Pagination ordering and limit handling are present. PASS
src/Routes/V1/CommentsRoutes.go GET /comments/list-like/:commentSid is registered to the intended controller/action. Route mapping matches the API contract. PASS

White, gray, and black-box coverage

Method Scenario Result
White-box Inspected the aggregate-count branch and compared its behavior with the UI continuation convention. Pass for populated pagination pages
Gray-box Exercised real authenticated requests using the client-shaped headers, query parameters, and response envelope. Pass: 5 + 1 users and aggregate remains 6
Black-box Checked public success, final partial page, private resource, missing auth, and unknown resource behavior. Pass

Confusion matrix — private visibility access control

Actual visibility API decision Expected deny Expected allow
Private post comment Deny (403) 1 (true positive) 0 (false positive)
Public post comment Allow (200) 0 (false negative) 1 (true negative)

This matrix is applicable to the visibility authorization rule. It is not applicable to the pagination aggregate defect, which is a deterministic data-consistency assertion.

Conclusion

The private-visibility guard, list response, and pagination behavior work as intended. The earlier empty-page concern was reclassified after live validation: it is the FE continuation convention, not a coding bug. No HTTP 500 was observed.
